headline: Central Bank of Nigeria authorizes banks to sell $1 million to BDCs
summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria has approved banks to sell up to $1 million in cash to Bureau De Change (BDC) operators. The measure aims to increase physical dollar liquidity in the retail foreign exchange market effective November 25, 2026.
why: Nigeria has been struggling with currency volatility and a shortage of foreign exchange. This intervention is a direct attempt to stabilize the retail FX market and support the naira.

impacts.name: Nigerian Naira
impacts.why: Increased dollar liquidity is intended to support the local currency value.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The policy change is designed to address the scarcity of foreign currency in the retail market, which has pressured the naira.
